Upon the successful commissioning of the pilot, Erik Meuleman, Ph.D., Chief Technology Officer, became the Principal Investigator for the Award. Dr. Meuleman has over 30 years of experience in technology development in chemical engineering and separation processes. He has led numerous multi-million-dollar innovation projects with international, multi-disciplinary teams based in Europe, Brazil, Australia, Japan, China, and the United States. Since his start at ION in January 2016, he has been responsible for all research activities, including ION’s successful campaigns at TCM and NCCC. As the PI for this part of the project, he provided technical oversight and direction and was responsible for completing all project objectives. ION Clean Energy 3 DE-FE0031950: FINAL PROJECT REPORT Figure 2-1: Project Organizational Chart In Budget Period 1 (BP1), ION generated the design documents for the construction team, including an overall Heat and Material Balance for the pilot system at design conditions and under turndown. ION led the Process Design Review (PDR) and Hazardous Operations (HAZOP) meetings, as well as oversaw equipment selection for both the CO Island and the balance of plant. In Budget Period 2 2 (BP2), ION oversaw solvent procurement, CO Island fabrication, and acceptance testing. In 2 Budget Period 3 (BP3), ION operated the pilot facility and analyzed all project data, culminating in this Final Report deliverable to the DOE and project partners. KMPS incorporated its own engineering expertise with ION’s innovative solvent to produce a Process Design Package that included P&IDs, a 3D-model, and equipment specifications. Together, these documents formed the basis for the PDR and HAZOP meetings. In BP2, KMPS fabricated, tested, and transported the modules to the site for installation by S&L. KMPS and S&L ensured the scope was clearly defined and the takeoff points were all identified. S&L was responsible for BOP for all utilities (flue gas, electricity, steam, cooling water, foundation, and communication). They collaborated directly with Calpine to deliver all utilities to the pilot modules. S&L also oversaw the final module installation and connections to BOP in BP2. Additionally, S&L performed the Preliminary and Final Techno-Economic Assessment of the ION ION Clean Energy 4 DE-FE0031950: FINAL PROJECT REPORT solvent and process technology integrated into a greenfield NGCC facility for direct comparison to DOE’s base case. Calpine provided the host facility for the pilot plant. They supported ION and KMPS by providing site-specific flue gas and utility specifications integral to the CO Island design. Calpine also 2 spearheaded site permitting based on emissions data for the ION carbon capture technology. Calpine’s engineers and operators provided key, site-specific insight during the PDR and HAZOP review. During BP3, Calpine provided engineering and operations support while ION personnel operated the pilot facility. ION acted as the project lead and was responsible for bringing all parties together as necessary to ensure that the project objectives were met in a timely manner.
